subject: Medford High School Building Project Alternatives
overview: The School Committee hosted its third community meeting to provide an update on the Medford High School building project and review the six remaining design alternatives. The project team detailed the feasibility study schedule, educational programming for a comprehensive high school, and the financial trade-offs between renovation and new construction.

items.title: Project Schedule and MSBA Submission Timeline
items.summary: Matt Gulino outlined the project timeline, noting the feasibility study is halfway complete and the Preferred Schematic Report is due to the MSBA by June 25, 2026.

items.title: PDP vs. PSR Feasibility Study Phases
items.summary: Matt Rice described the transition to the Preferred Schematic Report phase, which involves detailed floor plans, site grading calculations, and total carbon assessments.

items.title: Review of Six Design Alternatives
items.summary: The project team presented six options narrowed from an original 29, including mandatory code repairs, structure-preserving additions, and new construction on the parking lot or Edgerly Field.

items.title: Comprehensive High School and Community Services
items.summary: Suzanne Galusi and Jenny Graham discussed the necessity of housing vocational programs and community-facing services like the Medford Family Network and municipal daycare within the new design.

items.title: Modular Classrooms and Construction Phasing
items.summary: The team explained that renovation options would require up to 56 modular classrooms to maintain academic and vocational instruction during the four-year construction period.

items.title: High-Rise Construction and Pool Funding
items.summary: Matt Rice noted that six-story designs trigger high-rise building code premiums and clarified that new construction options require a separate ballot vote for pool funding.

items.title: Upcoming Milestones and Outreach
items.summary: The committee reviewed upcoming key dates, including the April 27 building committee meeting and the scheduled selection of a preferred alternative on June 10.
